questions.question: LPARA_REQ_W has 'at least 7' minimum, but the formula ADDR_W + 3 + 1 + STRB_W + DATA_W gives a minimum of 1+3+1+1+8 = 14; is the stated minimum correct? Similarly, LPARA_RESP_W minimum 9 equals DATA_W+1 at DATA_W=8 and is consistent.
questions.note: The document is internally inconsistent. The formula ADDR_W+3+1+STRB_W+DATA_W gives a minimum of 14 for ADDR_W=1 and DATA_W=8, but 'at least 7' is stated. The designer must say whether the stated minimum or the formula is correct. (LPARA_RESP_W minimum 9 is consistent.)

decision.answer: The formula is binding: LPARA_REQ_W = ADDR_W + 3 + 1 + STRB_W + DATA_W (+ USER_REQ_W + USER_DATA_W in APB5) and LPARA_RESP_W = DATA_W + 1 (+ USER_DATA_W + USER_RESP_W in APB5), as in the parameter table and section 9. 'At least 7' is a loose lower bound that every legal configuration satisfies (the formula gives at least 14), not a separate requirement; no check is made on it. Both widths are internal and not visible at the ports.

questions.question: Assertions are disabled while either reset is asserted, yet SVA-016 must hold in reset and SVA-007 must hold 'in reset'. Which reset (requester or completer, or both) enables SVA-016 and SVA-007?

It does not say which reset (mst, slv, or both) enables SVA-016, or what applies to SVA-007 in reset. The designer must resolve this.

decision.answer: SVA-016 (REQ-RESET-001: 'while one is asserted, every flip-flop of its domain shall be at its reset value') is checked per domain: while i_rst_n_mst = 0 the mst-domain outputs (o_apb_pready, o_apb_prdata, o_apb_pslverr, o_apb_pruser, o_apb_pbuser) are at their reset values; while i_rst_n_slv = 0 the slv-domain outputs (o_apb_psel, o_apb_penable, o_apb_pwrite, o_apb_paddr, o_apb_pprot, o_apb_pstrb, o_apb_pwdata, o_apb_pwakeup, o_apb_pauser, o_apb_pwuser) are at their reset values, sampled on the clock of that domain. SVA-007 is an ordinary assertion (disabled while either reset is asserted, section 15.3); its 'in reset' part is the slv-domain part of SVA-016 (o_apb_psel and o_apb_penable are 0 in reset).

questions.note: The values are given: for N=2, T_mst=10 ns and T_slv=20 ns, EXC-001 is 20 ns, EXC-002 20 ns, EXC-003 10 ns, EXC-004 10 ns and EXC-005 20 ns. 'The same two commands' means set_max_delay -ignore_clock_latency plus set_false_path -hold. However, whether the hold check is really disabled in a Synopsys sign-off tool (and the semantics and priority of the exceptions) is explicitly unconfirmed (OI-004).

decision.answer: Values accepted as computed by the specification for N = 2, T_mst = 10 ns, T_slv = 20 ns (EXC-001 20 ns, EXC-002 20 ns, EXC-003 10 ns, EXC-004 10 ns, EXC-005 20 ns; set_max_delay -ignore_clock_latency plus set_false_path -hold). Whether a sign-off tool disables the hold check is OI-004, a static timing item not verifiable by RTL simulation; no simulation check depends on it.

questions.question: OI-002/ASM-005: Which party guarantees the slv clock is running when a request arrives with a gated clock enabled only by PWAKEUP? It is an open item for the designer to clarify.
questions.note: The document says only that the slv clock controller must act on i_apb_pwakeup (or a requester signal) before the request arrives, and that ASM-005 assumes the controller keeps i_clk_slv running. OI-002 is still marked 'Clarify with the designer' and ASM-005 is Open. Missing: the designer's decision on which party guarantees the clock.

decision.answer: Integration assumption (ASM-005), outside the IP: the system clock controller guarantees i_clk_slv is running when a request arrives. The simulation keeps both clocks free running during transfers (except tests that stop a clock on purpose while the bridge is idle); no check is made on a gated completer clock.

questions.question: DEC-019 and DEC-020 are the author's choices and not confirmed by the designer. Should PREADY-only-in-RESP and response-after-handshake-closed be treated as binding for verification?
questions.note: The document does not say. DEC-019 and DEC-020 are the author's unconfirmed choices (the RTL was written with them), while REQ-FUNC-004 and REQ-HS-004 are written as 'shall'. Missing: designer confirmation of whether they are binding.

decision.answer: Binding for verification. The RTL was written with DEC-019 and DEC-020, and REQ-FUNC-004 (PREADY high for exactly one i_clk_mst cycle, in a cycle with PSEL and PENABLE high) and REQ-HS-004 (four-phase: PREADY only after the acknowledge returned to 0) are 'shall' requirements. A failure of these checks goes to triage for the designer; it is not waived.

questions.question: DEC-021 deviates from PRT-03 by declaring APB5 ports in all configurations. Does the designer accept this deviation, and does it conflict with the APB4 configuration in DEC-003?
questions.note: DEC-021 is the author's unconfirmed choice, and OI-005 asks the designer to confirm it or deliver two tops. The document does not record acceptance. It also does not settle whether it conflicts with DEC-003 (one parameter selects APB4/APB5). Missing: the designer's confirmation.

decision.answer: Accepted for verification as written (DEC-021): the APB5 ports exist in every configuration (width at least 1 for an absent user signal); with PARA_APBCDC_APB5 = 0 the APB5 inputs are ignored and the APB5 outputs are 0 (REQ-APB5-003). This does not conflict with DEC-003: the parameter still selects APB4 or APB5 behavior; only the port list is fixed. The PRT-03 deviation itself (OI-005) is a coding-rule item for the designer, not checked by simulation.

answered_questions.question: Feature FEAT-004 (four-phase) is Optional but PARA_APBCDC_HS_TYPE=1 selects it; confirm that the bridge is required to implement it when configured, and how HS_TYPE values other than 0/1 behave.
answered_questions.answer: Yes. FEAT-004 is optional only in the sense that it is present when PARA_APBCDC_HS_TYPE=1 is chosen. When selected, REQ-HS-001 makes the four-phase handshake mandatory. HS_TYPE values other than 0 or 1 are illegal and their behavior is not specified or checked.

answered_questions.question: PARA_APBCDC_CELL_TYPE 0 is 'simulation only': is it a legal configuration to verify, and what synchronizer behaviour is expected?
answered_questions.answer: CELL_TYPE=0 is inside the stated range 0 to 4. It means bypass with no synchronizer stage, for simulation only. It must not be used in a netlist, and the SDC rejects it (depth below 2). The test plan covers CELL_TYPE 1 to 4 only.

answered_questions.question: In the APB4 profile (PARA_APBCDC_APB5 = 0), are the APB5 signals (PWAKEUP, PAUSER, PWUSER, PRUSER, PBUSER) absent from the port list, or present and tied off? The quote does not say.
answered_questions.answer: The APB5 ports are present in every configuration of the RTL top. In APB4 the unused inputs are ignored and the unused outputs are 0, so they are tied off, not removed.

answered_questions.question: REQ-FUNC-007 says back-to-back Setup is accepted in the cycle after PREADY, but REQ-HS-004 (4-phase) raises PREADY only after ack returns to 0. In 2-phase, is the next Setup accepted immediately with the handshake still open? Is the PREADY timing the same in both modes?
answered_questions.answer: In both modes PREADY is a one-cycle pulse in state RESP, and the FSM then returns to IDLE and can capture the next Setup in the following cycle. In two-phase the acknowledge event itself leads to PREADY, and request and acknowledge are equal when idle. In four-phase PREADY is delayed until the acknowledge has fallen, so the handshake is closed before the next Setup. The PREADY pulse behaves the same in both modes. Only the latency differs.

answered_questions.question: REQ-IF-003 says outputs that need not be valid hold a stable value with reset value zero. Does 'stable' mean constant zero or hold last value? Does it cover completer-side outputs such as PADDR when idle?
answered_questions.answer: 'Stable' means the last value is held, not forced to zero. Registers reset to 0, PRDATA holds its value until the next response, and PSLVERR is cleared after the PREADY cycle. The completer-side fields such as PADDR keep the last bundle value when idle.

answered_questions.question: REQ-FUNC-001 requires PAUSER/PWUSER only in APB5, but REQ-FUNC-008 lists them as held signals for all configurations. Are they present only in APB5 configurations?
answered_questions.answer: PAUSER and PWUSER are functionally meaningful only in APB5 with a width above 0. The ports exist in the top in every configuration, and in APB4 they are ignored and the outputs are 0.

answered_questions.question: What exactly counts as 'a transfer in progress on the completer side' for o_apb_pwakeup, and when does it start and end?
answered_questions.answer: The term is the in-progress term of the completer-side FSM. o_apb_pwakeup is a flip-flop that must be high no later than o_apb_psel. It falls one cycle after the transfer ends, which is when psel and penable drop at the PREADY edge. It is high whenever the synchronized wake-up is high or a transfer is in progress.

answered_questions.question: What state is expected after a single reset is asserted, given it is unsupported, and is it to be tested at all?
answered_questions.answer: The state is not specified. A single reset is unsupported, is not detected, and is not tested. TEST-012 resets both domains together.

answered_questions.question: CFG-MIN lists 'Enabled features: CFG-APB4', which is a configuration ID, not a feature. Does CFG-MIN derive from CFG-APB4 (the rule's reading) or enable a feature named FEAT-xxx? Also, is ADDR_W 1 legal for an APB bridge?
answered_questions.answer: CFG-MIN derives from the configuration CFG-APB4. The other configurations use the same pattern ('CFG-APB4 plus ...'). ADDR_W=1 is legal, because the range is 1 to 32 and only 0 is illegal. CFG-MIN is the smallest legal instance.

answered_questions.question: Are the illegal combinations in Section 8 consistent with CFG-MIN (ADDR_W 1, DATA_W 8 with FEAT-004/006/007 absent)?
answered_questions.answer: Yes, they are consistent. ADDR_W=1 and DATA_W=8 are inside the legal ranges. The user widths are 0 with APB5=0, so none of the listed illegal combinations applies. FEAT-004, FEAT-006 and FEAT-007 are absent by parameters.

answered_questions.question: Is the one-cycle-after-PSEL PENABLE rule affected when the slv FSM sees a new request while in other states? Is PREADY zero-wait possible at Access entry?
answered_questions.answer: The slv FSM looks for a request event only in IDLE. SETUP always goes to ACCESS, and PENABLE rises one cycle after PSEL. A new request cannot arrive earlier, because APB is non-pipelined and the bridge carries one transfer at a time. A zero-wait PREADY in the first Access cycle is legal.

answered_questions.question: PWAKEUP, PRUSER and PBUSER are described in section 6.3 but are not in the port table. Does the bridge pass them through, and in which configuration?
answered_questions.answer: The premise is wrong, because these signals are in the port table. i_apb_pwakeup and o_apb_pwakeup are CFG-APB5 and cross through the synchronizer. PRUSER and PBUSER (i_ and o_) are CFG-USER and travel in the response bundle. They are passed through unchanged.

answered_questions.question: Does 'should provide all user signals' conflict with user ports existing only in CFG-USER?
answered_questions.answer: There is no conflict. 'Should provide all user signals' is a recommendation restated from REF-001. The bridge provides all four user signals in configurations with APB5=1 and width above 0. A width of 0 means the signal is not present.

answered_questions.question: The bridge forwards PSTRB as received, but PSTRB must be low in a read. Does the bridge check or force this, or just forward it?
answered_questions.answer: The bridge does not check or force PSTRB. It forwards PSTRB as received, including a non-zero value in a read, regardless of PWRITE.

answered_questions.question: Is the in-flight transfer loss on reset a requirement to check, and what must the outputs show afterwards, given that a single reset is unsupported?
answered_questions.answer: Yes. A transfer in flight at reset is lost, and both resets must be asserted together. While reset is asserted, every register is at its reset value. After release the test expects state cleared and the transfer repeated correctly (the repeat is done by the requester model).

answered_questions.question: Is the request/ack bit toggle or level? The quotes say 'toggle or level' without selecting one; this affects the 'request event' definition.
answered_questions.answer: It is selected by PARA_APBCDC_HS_TYPE. 0 gives toggle (two-phase) and 1 gives level (four-phase). The request event is: two-phase, synchronized request different from reg_ack (slv side); four-phase, synchronized request high. The ack event on the mst side is: two-phase, synchronized ack equal to reg_req; four-phase, synchronized ack high.

answered_questions.question: Is 7.3-04 an IP requirement or only a testbench requester assumption?
answered_questions.answer: It is an integration assumption outside the IP, not logic the IP implements. The resets are asserted together and released synchronously outside the IP. REQ-RESET-002 and ASM-002 state this, and there is no reset synchronizer inside. The testbench requester keeping PSEL low is only the verification model.

answered_questions.question: Legal USER_DATA_W is 0 to DATA_W, but the quote says an integer multiple of 8 is only recommended; are non-multiples legal?
answered_questions.answer: Yes, non-multiples of 8 are legal. The legal range is 0 to DATA_W, a multiple of 8 is only recommended, and non-multiples are not in the illegal list.

answered_questions.question: Rule AB2-8-01 says there is no elaboration check, while REQ-PARAM-001 is referenced; is any check expected for illegal values?
answered_questions.answer: No check is expected. The IP has no elaboration check for illegal values, and their behavior is unspecified. REQ-PARAM-001 only requires accepting the legal values, which are verified by elaborating the legal extremes.

answered_questions.question: In AB2-9-08 and AB2-9-09, is 'equal when idle' for two-phase mode defined for the request and acknowledge bits at reset as well as between transfers? What is the reset value?
answered_questions.answer: Yes, both are 0 at reset. In two-phase the request and acknowledge bits are equal when idle, and at reset both are 0. Between transfers they are equal and not necessarily 0. In four-phase both are 0 when idle.

answered_questions.question: OP-009 cites the bound of REQ-PERF-002 (four-phase), while OP-001 and OP-002 cite REQ-PERF-001 or REQ-PERF-002. Which bound applies in each mode? Section 10.4 gives separate formulas for the two handshakes.
answered_questions.answer: The bound follows the handshake type. HS_TYPE 0 uses REQ-PERF-001, (N+3)T_mst+(N+3+w)T_slv. HS_TYPE 1 uses REQ-PERF-002, (2N+4)T_mst+(2N+4+w)T_slv. OP-001 and OP-002 cite whichever applies to the configuration. OP-009 is the four-phase case, so REQ-PERF-002.

answered_questions.question: OP-006 gives the o_apb_pwakeup ordering as 'before or with o_apb_psel'. Is the wake-up term also required to stay high for the whole transfer, and what is the exact reset or deassertion behaviour?
answered_questions.answer: Yes. o_apb_pwakeup is high whenever the synchronized wake-up is high or a transfer is in progress. It stays high until PREADY when high with PSEL, falls one cycle after the transfer, and resets to 0.

answered_questions.question: Is the four-phase REQ0 or CLOSE return-to-zero phase included in the 4N+8+w total? How is it counted when the clocks are unequal?
answered_questions.answer: Yes, it is included. D is measured from Setup to the end of the PREADY cycle, and PREADY is raised only after the acknowledge has fallen (CLOSE/REQ0). The equal-clock figure 4N+8+w matches the measurement (16 for N=2). With unequal clocks the bound is the sum (2N+4)T_mst+(2N+4+w)T_slv.

answered_questions.question: AB2-12-01 and others use 'interconnect' as actor, but the quotes describe the bridge behavior. Which side (requester-facing or completer-facing) is the bridge treated as, and which actor label should be used?
answered_questions.answer: The document does not use 'interconnect'. The bridge is an APB completer on the requester-side interface and an APB requester on the completer-side interface. The behavior is attributed to the bridge or IP, and the requester model in the testbench.

answered_questions.question: For ERR-003, when a reset is asserted mid-transfer, are both resets required to be asserted together? Is the requester repeat part of the testbench model or a bridge requirement?
answered_questions.answer: Yes, both resets are asserted together, as REQ-RESET-002 requires. The repeat of the transfer is done by the requester model of the verification, not by the bridge. The bridge only loses the in-flight transfer.

answered_questions.question: N, w, T_mst and T_slv are not defined in the quotes (N likely synchronizer stages, w likely wait states or width). Define them and the measurement start and end points for the transfer duration. Does the limit include the PREADY wait time of the slave?
answered_questions.answer: N is the number of synchronizer stages (2, 2, 3, 4 for CELL_TYPE 1 to 4). w is the number of completer wait states. T_mst and T_slv are the clock periods. The duration D runs from the first cycle of the Setup phase to the end of the PREADY cycle on the requester side. The limit includes the wait states through the w term.

answered_questions.question: Does 'next Setup accepted in the cycle after PREADY' hold when the clocks differ and a synchronizer handshake is in progress? Which clock domain's cycle is meant (master or slave)? This seems to conflict with the multi-cycle duration limits in the other rules.
answered_questions.answer: It refers to the requester-side clock (i_clk_mst): the Setup is accepted in the cycle after the PREADY cycle. By then the handshake has completed, because PREADY is raised only after the acknowledge event (four-phase: after it has returned to 0). So it does not conflict with the multi-cycle duration limit, which is the time per transfer.

answered_questions.question: Is the actor for 14.1-07 (every flop async reset to 0) really absolute, given synchronizer cells have PARA_APBCDC_CELL_RST_VAL and library cells may differ?
answered_questions.answer: The rule holds. The wrapper reset value PARA_APBCDC_CELL_RST_VAL is 0 for all control bits of this IP. The synchronizer stages reset to 0, so every flop resets to 0.

answered_questions.question: What exactly is the deviation DEC-021 (PRT-03) from REF-003? It is unspecified, so conformance cannot be checked.
answered_questions.answer: DEC-021 is this: the RTL top declares the APB5 ports in every configuration, with widths of at least 1 for absent user signals, unused inputs ignored and unused outputs 0. This is because SystemVerilog has no optional ports. It deviates from PRT-03 and is recorded in the module header.

answered_questions.question: What are the numeric transfer-duration bounds of REQ-PERF-001 and REQ-PERF-002, and when does each apply? SVA-018 cannot be checked without them.
answered_questions.answer: Two-phase (HS_TYPE 0): duration at most (N+3)T_mst+(N+3+w)T_slv. Four-phase (HS_TYPE 1): at most (2N+4)T_mst+(2N+4+w)T_slv. They apply as in the answer to Q25, with N, w and T as defined for REQ-PERF-001/002. Example, equal clocks: 2N+6+w and 4N+8+w cycles.

answered_questions.question: Is the quick-run pass criterion (zero failures and every assertion hit at least once) actually stated? The quote is truncated.
answered_questions.answer: The quick run is reported with 64 runs, 0 failures, assertion failures 0 and assertions never exercised 0. The pass criterion is therefore zero failures and every assertion exercised at least once.

answered_questions.question: Both quotes begin with 'Not required (confirmed by user)', yet AB2-16-01 then uses 'shall'. Is the no-latch/no-comb-loop/no-tri-state/no-clock-gating/no-derived-clock restriction a binding requirement, or only a note that no DFT spec exists in this version?
answered_questions.answer: It is binding. 'Shall' is defined as mandatory and testable, and the sentence says the RTL shall contain no latch, combinational loop, tri-state, clock gating or derived clock. 'Not required' refers to the detailed DFT specification.

answered_questions.question: Is the absence of DFT ports (and the test-reset override being handled by the SoC wrapper per REF-003 RST-04) a binding requirement on the IP, or only a statement that DFT is out of scope?
answered_questions.answer: It is binding through the port list. The IP has no DFT ports and the port list has no test ports, and REQ-IF-001 requires exactly the ports of 6.2. The test-reset override belongs to the SoC wrapper.

answered_questions.question: The guard band is 'one destination period' and the post-CTS latency difference limit is tied to it. Which destination clock applies in each direction?
answered_questions.answer: The guard band is one period of the destination clock of each crossing. For mst-to-slv crossings it is T_slv, and for slv-to-mst crossings it is T_mst. That is why the budgets are (N-1)xT_slv for the request bundle and (N-1)xT_mst for the response bundle.
